project.topic: What if social media didn't exist for 5 seconds in 2026?
project.title: What if social media didn't exist for 5 seconds in 2026?
project.audience: Curious international viewers; a playful technology thought experiment in one cafe.
project.core_question: What do you save when your social audience vanishes for five seconds?
project.viewer_takeaway: A temporary disappearance of social platforms need not disable the internet, SMS or a local camera. In this individual cafe story, a failed tap redirects attention to a real near-miss and an optional post.

captions.style: Inter Bold uppercase impact phrases with dark outline and shadow, 2-5 words, max two balanced lines
captions.active_word_treatment: Active word in solar yellow #FACC15 with a subtle scale lift.
captions.highlights_policy: The physical consequence of each scene in accent colour; at most two emphasis phrases per scene.

audio.voice_style: Crisp, urgent, fascinated adult male; high-tension simulation narrator; brisk opening cadence
audio.music_direction: Original playful micro-thriller: digital plucks drop away, light physical percussion carries the sliding cup, a 0.3-second silence drop precedes the catch, then a warm conversational motif replaces the online pulse.
audio.sfx_direction: Physical glass taps, cup skimming wood, a soft ceramic catch and set-down, a restrained return notification and a final phone-case contact. No catastrophe or invented alarm.

scientific_model.baseline_reality: Social platforms are software services accessed over wider networks. A smartphone also has local functions and carrier SMS. A platform outage is not synonymous with the entire internet disappearing.
scientific_model.counterfactual_change: In a chosen ordinary 2026 cafe, every social app, social website, feed, livestream and platform direct-message service temporarily vanishes from use for exactly five seconds. Their saved state returns at second five. This is a stipulated temporary disappearance, not a historical world without social media.
assumptions: Keep electricity, the internet, carrier networks, ordinary SMS, local camera/storage, memories and physical laws unchanged. Platform DMs disappear; ordinary SMS is explicitly separate.
Accounts and data are preserved, and the unfinished local draft remains. Exact five-second restoration is part of the hypothetical, not a promise about real outage recovery.

The 48-second film expands a five-second event. One continuous HUD outage clock is derived from the same explicit film-to-story time mapping used by the cup and people; after restoration it stays at 5.00 seconds.
The user has nudged a partly filled coffee toward a raised table edge while posting. This is one authored cafe accident, not an effect suffered by everyone or a claim that an outage changes gravity.

The cup stays supported by the table edge and then by a hand. It never hangs in free fall while phone checks occur. The partly filled cup is caught before a spill. Contact animation is illustrative, not a fluid-dynamics forecast.
The friend is present across the table from the opening. Pointing, laughter, rescue and choosing not to post are individual fictional actions, not a measured psychological or social response.

Generic original phone UI represents the stipulated functions; no actual 2026 platform inventory, branded interface, notification count or usage statistic is asserted. The camera preview is rendered from the real 3D stage.
causal_chain: A posting attempt loses all social access while the already nudged cup continues sliding.
Working camera and SMS distinguish the stipulated platform disappearance from a broken phone or whole-internet blackout.
A failed repeat tap and the friend pointing redirect attention to the approaching table edge.
A supported hand catches the cup, preserving the drink; the friend reacts.
At second five the apps and unfinished draft return, creating a concrete choice.
The user sets the phone face down and leaves this shared moment unposted.
uncertainties: No population-wide panic, economic loss, mental-health benefit or habit change is inferred from five seconds.
Real platform outages have dependency failures and recovery complexity; this fictional restoration removes those uncertainties by stipulation.
The incident, low-friction slide and performance are authored; exact contact states are checked, but no rigid-body solver or liquid-volume model is claimed.

claims.statement: Social access disappears for exactly five story seconds and returns with saved state.
claims.reasoning: This is the explicit user counterfactual interpreted as temporary loss of social services, with preservation and exact restoration chosen as scenario rules.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Do not call this a real 2026 event or erase memories/history. The HUD counts story seconds, not the 48-second film duration.

claims.statement: Losing a platform does not inherently mean losing every network or local phone function.
claims.reasoning: Meta describes how its own backbone and DNS failures disconnected its services from the broader internet. Apple documents the local Camera app; Twilio distinguishes SMS from app messaging. Holding unaffected infrastructure constant defines this scenario.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Do not claim every real outage leaves all dependent services unaffected. Social DMs vanish here; carrier SMS and local camera are separately stipulated to survive.

claims.statement: An ordinary SMS message and a local camera can remain usable in this chosen social-platform disappearance.
claims.reasoning: Carrier SMS is a separate communication channel and local capture is a device function. The scenario explicitly keeps their networks, hardware and storage intact.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Say SMS, not all messages. Do not claim RCS, social login or cloud-dependent services are unaffected. No real messages are sent; the entire scene is CGI.

claims.statement: A sliding cup can still reach a table edge while a person is distracted by their phone.
claims.reasoning: Ordinary physical motion is held constant. A partly filled cup has been nudged in this individual authored example. Its support moves from tabletop to edge to the catching hand.
claims.presentation_guardrail: No floating free-fall cup, altered gravity, inevitable universal accident or guaranteed spill. Keep contacts and the supported completed state coherent.

claims.statement: A friend can point, laugh at the rescue, and share a moment the user chooses not to post.
claims.reasoning: These are illustrative individual character choices used to tell this fictional five-second story; they are not evidence of population behavior.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Remove invented habitual flaws and moral claims. Do not describe five seconds as a dopamine reset or social cure.

creative_direction.logline: Your audience vanishes for five seconds. The coffee heading for the table edge does not care.
creative_direction.visual_identity: One tactile 3D cafe, a real supported phone with diegetic UI and live rendered camera, an expressive seated friend and a ceramic near-miss.
creative_direction.lighting: Warm window key and cool plaster bounce with a phone glow kept readable; physical table shadows and controlled highlights. Single pipeline tone mapping.
creative_direction.camera_language: Eye-height over-table views, phone closeups, a friend-to-cup eyeline cut and a stable catching view. Return to the opening table for the final deliberate set-down.
creative_direction.motion_language: All motion uses absolute film time and the shared five-second story clock. The cup is supported throughout; hands meet physical phone and cup targets, release, and settle.
creative_direction.world_scale_policy: Metre-scale cafe and phone. The five-second event is expanded in film time and metered continuously; no world population maps or fabricated social metrics.
creative_direction.opening_hook: A posting tap loses its social screen as the nudged coffee visibly slides toward the edge.
creative_direction.mid_video_rehook: Before the midpoint, a friend points at the cup: this problem needs a hand rather than followers. The viewer redirects attention from a failed tap to a supported physical rescue.
creative_direction.ending_payoff: The apps and unfinished draft return at second five. The user chooses to set the phone face down beside the saved coffee and leave the shared moment unposted.
creative_direction.loop_connection: A final physical phone contact answers the opening digital tap. The saved cup occupies the same table as the original near-miss, with no spoken rewind instruction.
creative_direction.asset_policy: Reuse the registered room furnishings, mug, Humanoid/CharacterMotion, Modeling helpers and production pipeline. Only a generic phone case/UI and small facial details are story-specific.
